summary: The main implementation risks are lifecycle ownership between watchdog threads and asyncio, the missing structured Fireflies payload boundary, and conflicts between the requested file-only skills and the mixin’s default database registry. Confirmation idempotency, registry correlation, dependency packaging, and adversarial watcher tests also need explicit contracts.

suggestions.title: Define one asyncio owner for InboxWatcher
suggestions.rationale: InboxProcessor.run() is async and owns the writer lock, while watchdog callbacks execute in observer threads; the current CLI only bridges one coroutine with _run(). Require start() to capture the loop, callbacks to use call_soon_threadsafe(), one debounced worker task, and stop() to stop/join the observer and await the worker. No watchdog callback should invoke asyncio.run() or call InboxProcessor directly.

suggestions.title: Expose a structured Fireflies meeting payload
suggestions.rationale: The existing sync path fetches transcript and summary inside _sync_via_titles/_sync_via_registry, appends the native summary into one markdown string, and returns note titles rather than the raw inputs. A new agent cannot reliably satisfy C5 by calling sync_fireflies_transcripts and then analyzing its report. Introduce a Pydantic payload containing id, transcript, summary, metadata, and fingerprints; make the inbox writer and insight generator consume that same object.

suggestions.title: Specify the atomic-write and startup-scan contract
suggestions.rationale: InboxProcessor.discover() skips dot-prefixed files but otherwise accepts stable files recursively. If the agent’s temporary file has a visible name and remains for longer than the quiescence window, the watcher can ingest it before rename. The watcher also needs an initial recursive scan so files created while it was stopped are not lost. Require hidden or explicitly excluded temporary names, final-path revalidation, rename handling, and a startup scan.

suggestions.title: Make quiescence an injectable timing policy
suggestions.rationale: InboxConfig currently has no stability setting, and processor discovery reads files immediately. A single hard-coded sleep does not make the required two identical size+mtime observations deterministic or testable. Add a clearly named stability policy (window or poll interval plus sample count), compare nanosecond mtime and size, and inject the clock/stat source in tests so partial-write and slow-source cases run without real delays.

suggestions.title: Resolve watchdog’s optional-dependency packaging gap
suggestions.rationale: watchdog is declared in ai-parrot only under the filesystem-transport-full optional extra, not in the base dependency list. A core bot or ordinary wikitoolkit inbox invocation that imports the watcher can therefore fail on a normal ai-parrot install. Either make the watcher import lazy with a clear feature error and document the required extra, or add a narrowly scoped feature extra and enforce it in deployment tests.

suggestions.title: Add a genuine file-only mode to SkillRegistryMixin
suggestions.rationale: SkillRegistryMixin.enable_skill_registry defaults to true; its configure path creates a database-backed SkillRegistry persisted under AGENTS_DIR/{agent_id}/skills before configuring the file registry. Supplying skill_paths does not disable that database path, contradicting C3’s explicit no-DB requirement. Add a separate file-only configuration path or decouple file-registry setup from database-registry setup, and pin the agent id/path so it resolves exactly to fireflies_insights.

suggestions.title: Create an explicit ingestion-to-meeting correlation contract
suggestions.rationale: InboxProcessor detects fireflies:<id> and persists source metadata, while MeetingRegistry stores meeting state separately. Its mark_wiki_ingested() method only stamps rows and does not return the generated document or markdown path. A watcher may finish after Telegram insight delivery, so a Jira backlink cannot depend on timing. At confirmation time, resolve the shared registry/source manager by external id and persist or return a deterministic wiki-page path; alternatively add a post-ingest callback carrying fireflies_id, doc id, and markdown path.

suggestions.title: Treat Telegram confirmation as an idempotent authorization protocol
suggestions.rationale: telegram_command only attaches slash-command metadata; GitHubReviewer demonstrates proactive sending but has no approval state machine. The design must define an opaque insight id, channel and user authorization, expiry, rejection, replay behavior, and a durable or registry-backed created-ticket marker. Without this, a retried confirmation can create duplicate Jira issues, while a process restart silently loses pending approvals.

suggestions.title: Give working memory an explicit per-meeting scope
suggestions.rationale: WorkingMemoryToolkit is a tool-backed catalog with an optional session_id; BasicAgent only auto-wires it during configure(). The agent should create one shared toolkit per run, use stable keys such as meeting:<fireflies_id>:transcript and :summary, and define cleanup/isolation between meetings. Otherwise one meeting’s artifacts can leak into the next or the LLM may only see summaries without a deterministic way to retrieve the intended payload.

suggestions.title: Add failure-isolation and long-running CLI acceptance tests
suggestions.rationale: The existing inbox tests exercise CLI forwarding and lock behavior, but the processor tests contain placeholder assertions and there is no watcher contract coverage. Add deterministic tests for partial writes, identical size with changed mtime, atomic rename, startup discovery, burst coalescing, cancellation, InboxLockBusy, stage_git=false, and cleanup. Add end-to-end isolation cases proving insight delivery survives ingest failure and ingest survives insight failure, plus repeated Telegram confirmation and 4096-character escaped HTML cases.
